_doc: Which open-weight model plays which role when OTARI_API_KEY is set (verdict_desk/llm.py). Every id is a catalog id of the hosted Otari gateway, so Otari picks the provider and falls back across offerings of the same model. Checked against the public catalog (GET /api/v1/catalog/models) by tools/otari_catalog_check.py: each id must exist and be open_weights.
_policies_doc: Routing policies created once in the Otari dashboard, one per role that needs a fallback chain of our own. Used as the `model` of that role only when use_policies is true (or OTARI_USE_POLICIES=1); OTARI_POLICY_<ROLE> names one for a single role, for a drill. Without them the catalog id keeps Otari's automatic fallback across offerings of the same model.
_cycle_doc: The app's own spend caps for one decision cycle, in USD, each the sum of usage.cost_usd of the calls so far: `cycle_cap_usd` for the roles that argue, rule, check and read headlines (bull, bear, judge, checker, narrator), and `tool_cap_usd` for the roles that only drive an Otari tool (searcher, fetcher, sandbox, mcp), so a tool that costs a cent a call can never use up the money the analysts and the judge need. No new call starts once a cap is reached; calls already started finish. Each refusal is a client-side receipt (code cycle_cap_exceeded). OTARI_CYCLE_CAP_USD and OTARI_TOOL_CAP_USD override.
_send_user_doc: true now that the key is a service key. With an ordinary key Otari answers 403 "'user' field does not match the authenticated API key's user" (docs/FEEDBACK_LOG.md, entry 2).

rejected.meta/llama-4-scout-17b: planned as the citation checker, but on 2026-11-01 four of five tiny calls answered 504 from CloudFront after 30 s and the fifth took 23 s (docs/FEEDBACK_LOG.md, entry 2)

_end_user_doc: Each role is billed to its own end user (`vd-bull`, `vd-bear`, `vd-judge`, `vd-checker`, `vd-narrator`). `end_user_budget` is the id of the dashboard budget `vd-analyst` (USD 0.10 a day per end user); it travels in the Otari-End-User-Budget header and applies when an end user is first created. The panel's `vd-drill-tiny` is `drill_budget`; `drill_user` is the end user the budget drill bills.
_features_doc: Otari tools the app uses in a decision cycle: one web search (about USD 0.01 a call), one MCP price read (the public CoinGecko server, free) and one sandbox re-derivation per dossier (about USD 0.01 a call). The roles searcher, sandbox and mcp run the model that drives the tool; they share the judge's model on purpose (the one tool loop we measured end to end) and bill to their own end users. OTARI_WEB_SEARCH, OTARI_CODE_EXECUTION and OTARI_MCP set to 0 or 1 override.
_market_doc: `market_check_limit_pct`: the most the MCP spot price may differ from the exchange close before the packet's freshness is marked not ok and the verdict refuses to decide (fail closed). A missing or untrusted MCP price blocks nothing.
_judge_route_doc: The judge is routed by a deterministic rule sealed with its ruling (llm.judge.route_rule). A hard case (the deterministic bull and bear scores less than `margin_below` apart, the most a judge's vote can add, or `claims_at_least` validated claims, the most the analysts can bring) goes to `hard_model`, the larger DeepSeek, sent by its catalog id (Otari falls back across its providers); every other case goes to the standard judge, the vd-judge policy. No dashboard policy is created for it, and the hard route does not pass through vd-judge's guardrail. OTARI_JUDGE_ROUTE=0 turns the rule off.
_models_open_weights_doc: Whether each id that can appear as a receipt's sent_model is an open-weight model: every role's catalog id (flag on the role, checked by tools/otari_catalog_check.py), the larger judge, and the two routing policies, which only list open DeepSeek models.
_canary_doc: Every decision cycle starts with a failover canary before it trusts the judge: one small, honest call through the routing policy `drill_policy` (vd-judge-drill), whose main model has a 32k-token context and whose backup is DeepSeek. The prompt is filler long enough to overflow that context, so Otari must move to the backup. The receipt (attempt_count 2, fallback true) is sealed in the dossier under llm.otari.canary, labeled as a canary. If the backup did not take over, the cycle records it and the judge stays on the standard route. OTARI_CANARY=0 turns it off.
_headroom_doc: Budget-aware routing: each cycle reads, free, what Otari says each end user has spent (GET /end-users) and seals it as llm.otari.headroom. The hard judge route (judge_route) is allowed only while the judge's end user has used less than `headroom_max_fraction` of `end_user_limit_usd` (the day limit of the dashboard budget vd-analyst, USD 0.10; the service key cannot read the limit, so it is stated here). Unreadable state keeps the standard route.
